site.title: GitHub Inside Out
site.tagline: An unofficial field guide in four tracks
site.disclaimer: Independent learning material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by GitHub. Legal and tax notes are general information, not advice for your situation.

lenses.label: Legal & tax
lenses.blurb: Redlines, audit trails, chain of custody, workpapers.

tools.label: Phone
tools.blurb: GitHub Mobile or a mobile browser

tools.label: Command line
tools.blurb: git and gh in a terminal

tracks.title: Basics
tracks.subtitle: Foundations
tracks.promise: Build the mental model and the daily loop: commit, branch, sync, pull request.
tracks.audience: You have an account and a repository. The vocabulary is still fuzzy in places.

tracks.title: Intermediate
tracks.subtitle: Collaboration
tracks.promise: Work with other people without stepping on toes: conflicts, review, planning, undo.
tracks.audience: You can commit, push and pull. Branching with others and merge conflicts still feel risky.

tracks.title: Advanced
tracks.subtitle: Automation and guardrails
tracks.promise: Make the right thing the easy thing: Actions, protection rules, security, history surgery.
tracks.audience: You are comfortable with branches and pull requests. You want the machine to do the checking.

tracks.title: Expert
tracks.subtitle: Internals, scale and governance
tracks.promise: Know how it works underneath and how to run it for a team, an organization or a research group.
tracks.audience: You automate confidently. You want the internals, the failure modes and the rules of the road.
